text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT TENDER - Jordan is scheduled to tender July 23 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter or hard red spring wheat or equivalent wheat from other countries, U.S. exporters said. Half of the tonnage was slated for last-half August shipment and the balance for last-half September shipment.

CORN/SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said it wanted to buy 30,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine No. 2 yellow corn for arrival in the second half of September and/or the second half of October and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin, for arrival first half of October and/or first half of November. The deadline for the corn and soybean bids is noon (0900 GMT) July 22, he told Reuters.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp on July 15 will seek 40,000 tonnes of No.1 soybeans. It seeks 20,000 tonnes for September 20 arrival at Inchon and 20,000 tonnes for arrival by October 20.

RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.

CORN TENDER - South Korea will seek 50,000 tonnes of corn to be delivered to famine-threatened North Korea, the state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp said. Bids were due at 0300 GMT Saturday. Shipments will be made in August in lots of 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes each to North Korea's port of Nampo.

VEGETABLE OIL TENDER - Egypt's state Holding Company for Food Industries on July 16 will seek 25,000 to 40,000 tonnes of cottonseed, sunflower seed and soybean oils for delivery in August. The tender includes 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of crude sunflower seed oil and/or semi-refined cotton seed oil and/or American cottonseed oil PBSY 162 for arrival in the first half of August, 1997. - The same amounts and types of oil for second-half August arrival. Also, 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of degummed soybean oil second-half August arrival.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the agency's forecast of an unexpectedly large winter wheat crop earlier Friday would lead to aggressive export sales, but would not say whether the department would reactivate its wheat export subsidy program. "It increases our desire to move this wheat as aggressively as we can," Glickman told reporters, referring to the 1.78 billion bushel crop estimate. That projection is up 11 percent from the USDA's previous forecast, and 20 percent higher than last year's crop.
